evidence.description: Only the response data is retained; the response metadata is discarded.

candidates.explanation: The network response is discarded, so fetchAndUpdate does not distinguish successful HTTP responses from error responses before decoding and applying their bodies. A non-success response containing decodable statistics can therefore update the stored state.
candidates.title: HTTP response status is not validated

evidence.description: The actor method suspends while fetching data, allowing other calls to enter the actor.
Tree statistics and their timestamp are overwritten without a freshness comparison.
Investment statistics and their timestamp are also overwritten without a freshness comparison.

candidates.explanation: Actor isolation does not serialize the entire operation across the network await. Multiple calls can have requests in flight simultaneously, and an earlier request that completes later can overwrite statistics already updated by another call. The supplied last-updated timestamps are assigned without checking whether they are older than the stored timestamps.
candidates.title: Overlapping fetches can overwrite newer statistics

evidence.description: A failed numeric or date conversion skips the tree update without reporting the failure.
Invalid numeric strings fall back to the existing values.
Failed investment conversions likewise skip the update silently.

candidates.explanation: Conversion failures for recognized statistics are silently ignored. Unlike network or JSON decoding failures, invalid numeric values or timestamps do not produce an error: the method returns successfully while retaining old values, potentially leaving a mixture of refreshed and stale statistics with no indication that part of the update failed.
candidates.title: Invalid statistic values silently produce partial updates
